# #1760: Patch: the Duos gate measures the co-op AI against a greedy team, not only a random one
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The co-op AI's quality gate — the check that decides whether a change to the team AI is allowed — only ever plays opponents who pick random moves. Any regression that is merely bad rather than broken still beats random play, so the gate cannot see it. After the change the gate also plays a greedy team, the way the 1v1 gate already does.

## Why

The 1v1 gate measures three matchups — Random, Greedy, and Hard-vs-Easy (`crates/tools/src/gate.rs:212-221`). The Duos gate's only opponent is `duos_random_action`, the spec's random policy (`crates/ai/src/duos.rs:558-576`, used at `duos.rs:753`), at `DUOS_GATE_WIN_FLOOR: 0.8` (`config.rs:53-59`). A degraded `pass_gain` ordering or a teammate-probe bug — exactly the kind of feature #1723 shipped — is invisible to an opponent that never punishes it.

## Proposal

A `duos_greedy_action` built from the existing per-duel `greedy_action` (each seat greedily, sharing only what Duos seats may share), a second matchup in `duos_gate_game_at`, and its floor a named constant beside `DUOS_GATE_WIN_FLOOR`.

## Where it lands

`crates/ai/src/duos.rs` or `duos_gate.rs`, `crates/tools/src/duos_gate.rs`, `crates/ai/src/config.rs`; `cargo jackioh gate --duos`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `gate --duos` runs a greedy matchup alongside the random one
- [ ] Its win floor is a named constant in `config.rs`
- [ ] A deliberately weakened pass heuristic fails the greedy matchup (shown in a test or a documented run), where the random one cannot tell

## Size and risks

Small–medium — the pieces exist; the work is composing them and choosing an honest floor from measured runs rather than a guess.

## Goal

`cargo jackioh gate --duos` plays two matchups over the same game count: the Easy AI team against the random-policy team (unchanged) and against a team whose seats each play the 1v1 one-ply greedy baseline (`greedy_action`) in their own duel and never pass. The greedy matchup has its own floor, `DUOS_GATE_GREEDY_WIN_FLOOR = 0.7` in `crates/ai/src/config.rs`, set from measured runs. A daily test shows a deliberately weakened pass heuristic (each turn, before anything else, pass the first card the wrapper lets you pass) clearing the random floor and failing the greedy one.

**Planner's measurements** (scratch build of `51f86b343` with this design, run outside the worktree):

| AI team | vs random | vs greedy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| shipping, `duos-tune` 1–200 (fresh deals) | 200/200 | 168/200 (84%) |
| shipping, `duos-gate:v1` 1–20 (the CLI's) | 20/20 | 16/20 |
| shipping, `gate` 1–20 (the daily test's) | 20/20 | 19/20 |
| passes first card first, `duos-gate:v1` 1–20 | 20/20 | 9/20 |
| passes first card first, `gate` 1–20 | 20/20 | 7/20 |
| passes first card first, `duos-tune` 1–200 | 200/200 | 76/200 |

<!-- planner verification: this plan was applied in a scratch copy (/tmp/duos-impl): fmt --check, clippy -p jackioh-ai -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -D warnings clean; ai duos:: 51 passed; ai_slow duos_gate 7 passed + 3 daily passed (574 s); tools duos_gate 7 passed. -->


Every one of these runs had 0 refused actions, 0 fallbacks and 0 search panics. Binomial(20, 0.84) gives P(≤13 wins) = 0.03 and P(≤14) = 0.087, so 14 of 20 is the highest count an AI this strong reaches in 95% of runs (§9.9's rule): 0.7. Weakening only the ranking (never pass; pass everything; pass only the bad trades; dump every passable card at turn's end) won 160–167 of 200 against greedy, inside noise. The Easy AI team makes only 3–8 passes in 20 gate games, so no ranking change can show (see Open questions).

   ```rust
   /// B32's second opponent (#1760): the 1v1 gates' one-ply greedy baseline (`greedy_action`) on the
   /// seat's own duel. Its mulligan, prompts and turn are `greedy_action`'s, sent as a duel action when
   /// the wrapper offers that kind, else `duel_fallback`'s. It never passes: a yardstick that shared
   /// `duos_passes` would move with the AI it measures. It reads its duel through `greedy_action`'s
   /// `redact` alone (R185) and draws on `rng` only there. None when the seat has nothing to send.
   pub fn duos_greedy_action(state: &DuosState, seat: DuosSeat, rng: &mut Rng) -> Option<DuosActionBody> {
       if state.result.is_some() {
           return None;
       }
       let legal = duos_legal_actions(state, seat);
       if legal.iter().all(|body| matches!(body, DuosActionBody::Concede)) {
           return None;
       }
       let duel = state.duels.get(seat.duel())?;
       match greedy_action(duel, seat.player(), rng) {
           Some(action) if offers(&legal, action.action_type()) => Some(DuosActionBody::Duel { body: action }),
           _ => duel_fallback(&legal),
       }
   }
   ```

5. **Add `DuosOpponent`** just before `DuosGateReport`'s doc (line 598):
   ```rust
   /// B32: the team the Easy AI team plays in a gate game (#1760).
   #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
   #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
   pub enum DuosOpponent {
       /// Every seat on §10.7's random policy (`duos_random_action`).
       #[default]
       Random,
       /// Every seat on the one-ply greedy baseline (`duos_greedy_action`).
       Greedy,
   }

   impl DuosOpponent {
       /// The gate's matchups, in the order it plays them.
       pub const ALL: [DuosOpponent; 2] = [DuosOpponent::Random, DuosOpponent::Greedy];

       /// The share of its games the AI team must win against this team.
       pub fn win_floor(self) -> f64 {
           match self {
               DuosOpponent::Random => DUOS_GATE_WIN_FLOOR,
               DuosOpponent::Greedy => DUOS_GATE_GREEDY_WIN_FLOOR,
           }
       }

       /// Game n's seed: `${series}:${n}` against random (the seeds B32 always played), and
       /// `${series}:greedy:${n}` against greedy.
       pub fn seed(self, series: &str, n: usize) -> String {
           match self {
               DuosOpponent::Random => format!("{series}:{n}"),
               DuosOpponent::Greedy => format!("{series}:greedy:{n}"),
           }
       }

       /// This team's action for one of its seats, on that seat's stream.
       fn action(self, state: &DuosState, seat: DuosSeat, rng: &mut Rng) -> Option<DuosActionBody> {
           match self {
               DuosOpponent::Random => duos_random_action(state, seat, rng),
               DuosOpponent::Greedy => duos_greedy_action(state, seat, rng),
           }
       }
   }

   impl std::fmt::Display for DuosOpponent {
       fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
           f.write_str(match self {
               DuosOpponent::Random => "random",
               DuosOpponent::Greedy => "greedy",
           })
       }
   }
   ```

  /// #1760's weakened pass heuristic: once per round in its duel, before anything else, the seat passes
  /// the first card the wrapper lets it pass, whatever it is worth; otherwise it decides as the AI does.
  fn passes_its_first_card_first(state: &DuosState, seat: DuosSeat, options: &mut AiOptions<'_>) -> Option<DuosDecision> {
      let first = if state.passes.get(seat.duel()) == Some(&0) {
          duos_legal_actions(state, seat)
              .into_iter()
              .find(|body| matches!(body, DuosActionBody::Pass { .. }))
      } else {
          None
      };
      match first {
          Some(body) => Some(DuosDecision { body, fallback: false, sim_panics: 0, first_sim_panic: None }),
          None => duos_decision(state, seat, options),
      }
  }

## Risks

- **Replay and determinism**: random games keep their seeds and streams, so their results do not move. Greedy draws only on its own seat's `${seed}:ctl:${seat}` stream. Nothing reads a clock or the environment (rule 4).
- **Hidden information**: `greedy_action` reads through `redact`; greedy never passes, so it reads nothing of the teammate.
- **AI behaviour**: the `fallback` split must keep the AI's order exactly (EndTurn → `pass_or_end`). The `duos::` tests cover it.
- **Brittle seeds**: the daily tests sit on fixed seeds. Margins measured: 19 vs 14, 20 vs 16, 7 vs 14.
- **Unused import**: `DUOS_GATE_WIN_FLOOR` in tools' non-test code (Step 10).

## Open questions

- AC3 asked that a weakened pass heuristic fail the greedy matchup. Weakening the ranking (which cards it passes) cannot: the Easy AI team passes 3–8 times in 20 games, and the ranking variants won 160–167 of 200 against greedy (168 shipping).
